claims.text: Thermally activated super-jogging of edge dislocations limits dislocation mobility in refractory high-entropy alloys at elevated temperatures.
Super-jogging retards edge-dislocation glide.
Retarded edge-dislocation glide produces a high-temperature yield-strength plateau.
Retarded edge-dislocation glide produces a nearly temperature-independent elastic response.
NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 can be prepared as a homogenized, single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
Prolonged high-temperature homogenization eliminates segregation in the proposed alloy.
An intermediate-temperature anneal promotes recovery of the edge-dislocation network.
The anneal reduces the density or effective pinning of edge dislocations relative to the baseline.
The density and spatial distribution of edge dislocations govern the proposed mechanical and thermoelastic response.
Elevated-temperature plastic deformation in BCC NbTaTiV can be dominated by edge dislocations.
High strength and strength retention in NbTaTiV and CrMoNbV are attributable to edge dislocations.
The as-processed NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 baseline possesses a high density of pinned edge dislocations.
Reducing edge-dislocation density or pinning enhances dislocation mobility.
The recovered sample will exhibit a weaker high-temperature yield-strength plateau than the baseline.
The recovered sample will exhibit greater temperature dependence of yield strength than the baseline.
The recovered sample will exhibit greater temperature dependence of elastic modulus than the baseline.
High-vacuum testing precludes oxidation over the proposed 673–1073 K range.
High-load static nanoindentation produces a stress state similar to that encountered in intended high-temperature applications.
The controlled experiment compares identically composed as-processed and annealed specimens under constant loads above 1 N from 673 to 1073 K in high vacuum.
Indistinguishable mechanical responses in the two specimen sets would falsify edge-dislocation super-jogging as the governing mechanism.

contradictions.description: The uncertainty field allows that the annealing treatment may require optimization to modify the dislocation network clearly, whereas the falsification rule treats an indistinguishable response as falsifying the mechanism without first confirming that annealing actually changed dislocation density or pinning.
